izzyondroid:me.biplobsd.rsm.name: Running Services Monitor
izzyondroid:me.biplobsd.rsm.summary: Monitor running services on your Android device with Root or Shizuku
izzyondroid:me.biplobsd.rsm.description:
Running Services Monitor helps you monitor running services on your Android device. With a clean and intuitive interface, you can easily view system and user apps and check their status efficiently.
 Features 
 Monitor Running Services: View a comprehensive list of all running services on your device
 Categorized View: Easily switch between All, User, and System apps
 Search Functionality: Quickly find specific apps with the built-in search bar
 App Details: Get detailed information about each app, including package name, version, and more
 Root & Shizuku Integration: First checks for root permission, then falls back to Shizuku for advanced system interactions (where supported)
 Material Design 3: A modern and beautiful UI that adapts to your device's theme
 Dark/Light Mode: Toggle between dark and light themes for comfortable viewing
 Localization: Support for English, Bangla, Chinese languages
 Requirements 
 Essential:
 Android 7.0 (API 24) or higher
 Root access (preferred) OR Shizuku app installed and running
 Permissions:
 QUERY_ALL_PACKAGES - To list all installed apps
 Root permission OR Shizuku permission - The app first checks for root access, then falls back to Shizuku if root is unavailable
 How It Works 
 This app uses root access or Shizuku to execute privileged ADB commands. Starting from Android 8.0 (API 26), the ActivityManager.getRunningServices() API was deprecated and restricted. Third-party apps can no longer query all running services on the device for privacy and security reasons.
 Root access provides the most seamless experience with direct access to system commands and no additional setup required.
 Shizuku provides an alternative for non-rooted devices by running a privileged service that can access system APIs, allowing apps to execute ADB commands without root, working on non-rooted devices via Wireless Debugging (Android 11+) or USB ADB.
 The app checks for root permission first, and if not available, falls back to Shizuku. It executes dumpsys activity services to get running service information, parses the output to extract service details (package name, PID, process name, etc.), and categorizes services into System and User categories.
 Limitations 
 Due to Android security policies, some service information may be limited
 When using Shizuku, the service stops when device reboots
 Dumpsys output format may vary across Android versions
 This app only displays services; it cannot start/stop them
 This app is designed for users who want to monitor running services on their device, similar to the "Running Services" feature that was available in Android Developer Options in older Android versions.

fdroid:com.exner.tools.immichuploader.name: Immich Uploader
fdroid:com.exner.tools.immichuploader.summary: App that can upload media files to your Immich instance.
fdroid:com.exner.tools.immichuploader.description:
Immich Uploader is a small app that discovers media files on your Android device, then uploads them to your Immich instance.
 The app can be configured to remove media files from your device after successful updates. This can be configured individually by type of file (Photo, Screenshot, Download, or Others).
 It can also apply Tags to media files after successful upload. Again, this can be configured by type of file.
 Permissions
 Android
 The app needs INTERNET permissions for the upload as well as access to your media files, which it will explicitly ask for. 
 On devices running Android 17 or later, it also needs ACCESS_LOCAL_NETWORK permissions if you want to use a local server URL when your Android device is on the same network as your Immich server. This usually speeds up upload a great deal.
 Immich
 The app connects to your Immich instance. It needs an API Key to do so.
 You can use your standard Immich user, or you can (should) create a user specifically for Immich Uploader.
 The user must have the following permissions on your Immich instance:
 asset.upload - for uploading media assets
 apiKey.read - for testing the connection, used on the Settings screen (since v2.2.2)
 tag.read - for retrieving the list of Tags on your Immich instance (since v3.1.0)
 tag.asset - for applying Tags to assets (since v3.1.0)
 If you use the "Check connection" buttons on the Settings view, but your Immich user does not have apiKey.read permission, the check will fail.
 If your Immich user does not have tag.read permission, the app can not download Tags from the Immich instance, and if they do not have tag.asset permission, uploads will still work, but media files will not be tagged.

fdroid:com.redtrigger.name: RedTrigger
fdroid:com.redtrigger.summary: System-wide shoulder triggers for Nubia Red Magic phones
fdroid:com.redtrigger.description:
RedTrigger enables shoulder triggers (SAR capacitive sensors) on Nubia Red Magic phones system-wide, without needing Game Space.
Nubia's game framework controls the shoulder trigger hardware and only activates them inside Game Space. The system also resets trigger settings every time you switch apps. RedTrigger fixes both issues.
How it works:
- Activates SAR sensors without launching full Game Space
- Runs a watchdog service that detects when Nubia's SystemMgr resets trigger settings on app switch
- Re-applies settings instantly, keeping triggers active across all apps
Key remapping (via Shizuku):
- Reads raw input events from /dev/input using a Shizuku UserService
- Optionally injects remapped key events (L1/R1) so apps like KeyMapper can capture them
- Uses a virtual uinput device so remapped events appear as real hardware input
Requirements:
- Nubia Red Magic phone (tested on Red Magic 11 Pro)
- Shizuku installed and running (wireless ADB or root)
The app automatically grants itself WRITE_SECURE_SETTINGS via Shizuku, so no manual ADB commands are needed. Enable "Auto-enable on boot" to survive reboots.

fdroid:dev.midnightbeam.summary: Screen dimmer and warm filter for Android TV, with phone remote and schedule
fdroid:dev.midnightbeam.description:
Less blue light, more comfortable movie nights. MidnightBeam is a warm (red) filter and screen dimmer for Android TV boxes, projectors, TVs and phones.
It draws a click-through overlay above everything, video included. Filter strength, brightness and colour temperature change live, with no flash to full brightness. Made for the many LED projectors and TV boxes that cannot lower their own light.
 On the TV 
* a settings screen that needs only the D-pad and OK, with a clearly visible focus highlight
* a QR code to control it from a phone (the phone remote is on by default on TVs, on the local network only, protected by a pairing code; the TV announces itself there over mDNS so the phone app can find it)
* an "Android app" button with a QR code to download the app on a phone
* the schedule shown as a timeline at the bottom of the screen
 On a phone or tablet 
* use the filter on the phone itself, or control your TVs and projectors
* scenes (Movie, Relax, Night…) and your own, a power button and the state of every device
* add a TV by scanning its QR code or by hand (address and code); the device type is detected
* a guided setup for the permissions Android needs
* no app at all is needed for a quick try: the QR code opens the same controls in the phone browser
 Audio (optional) 
Volume, equalizer, presets, bass boost, surround and loudness of the device from the phone, with an on-screen display on the TV, on devices whose audio supports the standard Android effects.
 Schedule 
Daily or weekly time slots, dragged on a timeline, with gradual transitions between them; the TV applies them by itself, even with the phone off. A manual change lasts until the next slot.
 Automation 
* adb shell: am start-foreground-service -n dev.midnightbeam/.DimService --ei red 60 --ei bright 40 --ei temp 1100 
* Home Assistant, through the Android Debug Bridge integration (example package and dashboard in the source repository)
* a small HTTP API on the local network
The last setting is restored early at boot. The service can only be controlled by the app itself and from adb shell, not by other apps.
Plain Java, about 420 KB (mostly artwork), no trackers, no ads, no data collected, no internet connections: the network is used only on your local network, for the phone remote (port 8765) and to reach the TVs you paired.
The optional accessibility service is used only to draw the dimming overlay above everything on Android 12+; it reads no content.
On a TV box without a touch screen, the overlay permission can be granted with adb shell appops set dev.midnightbeam SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW allow , or in Settings, Special app access, Display over other apps.

debian-packages:checksecurity.name: checksecurity
debian-packages:checksecurity.description:
Checksecurity can periodically do some very basic system security checks:
 * check-setuid - scans for insecurely mounted remote file systems,
 and tracks changes in setuid programs;
 * check-sockets - tracks changes in open ports to detect rogue programs;
 * check-passwd - scans for empty or duplicate system accounts;
 * check-disfree - scans for mounted filesystems nearing capacity;
 * check-iptables-logs - scans logs generated by iptables and look
 for intrusion attempts.
Be aware that these minimal set of checks are no substitute for a full
security auditing and integrity checking system.
In addition to these checks you are encourage to install additional packages
(listed in "Recommends") to provide more information concerning the security
or vulnerability of your system.
Installing the suggested package lockfile-progs can help to prevent
the cron jobs running multiple times if something gets jammed.

firefox-addons:2998553.name: Privacy Thing (Preview)
firefox-addons:2998553.summary: See what a site checks and decide which browser data it receives — with separate rules for every website and Firefox container.
firefox-addons:2998553.description:
See more. Share less. 
Websites can learn far more about your browser than what you type into a form. They may read your geolocation, language, time zone, screen size, hardware characteristics, and other details about your environment. Even graphics information exposed through WebGL can become part of a recognizable browser fingerprint.
 Privacy Thing gives you practical control over this layer of privacy. It shows which browser information and features the page open in your browser accesses, then lets you decide which selected information it can see — separately for every website.
In Firefox, rules can also be assigned to containers. The same domain can therefore use a different profile depending on the context in which you open it.
 TL;DR 
 Privacy Thing lets you control the information your browser shares with websites and web apps.
 See which information a site used and how many times. 
 Create multiple sets of rules separately for every website and Firefox container.
 Create multiple location setups based on geographic position, available languages, and regional preferences. Privacy Thing includes a full-featured GPS-location spoofer with a realistic location-simulation model.
 Privacy Thing is built to provide as much functionality as possible without connecting to external services. Your settings remain yours.
 What Privacy Thing gives you 
 Reduce selected parts of your “digital fingerprint” — depending on the browser and configuration, Privacy Thing can control or modify selected information related to the browser, screen, and hardware, as well as canvas, WebGL, audio, WebRTC, frames, and workers. This includes some data that may reveal characteristics of the graphics hardware. Privacy Thing gives you a concrete set of tools for limiting and organizing information that falls within the extension’s reach.
 See what a site checks — X-Ray shows whether a site has accessed geolocation, language, screen data, canvas, WebGL, audio, WebRTC, or selected worker mechanisms. You can also see which profile was applied and whether any supported category encountered a problem. It is not a complete record of everything a website does. It is a practical view of the browser areas Privacy Thing can recognize and control.
 Set your own rules for every website — create profiles and assign them to domains or domain patterns. Use a default rule, add exceptions for particular websites, and temporarily switch Privacy Thing off without deleting your configuration. You can also use the extension only on selected websites — Privacy Thing does not restrict you to one operating model.
 Keep settings separate across Firefox Containers — assign different profiles to the same website depending on its container. This is a convenient way to keep work contexts, accounts, and use cases separate.
 Build coherent regional profiles — combine coordinates, geolocation accuracy and coordinate-variation radius, a primary language, a language list, and a time zone. The first-run wizard lets you quickly choose ready-made regional presets, while your own profiles remain freely editable. The Refract engine can align the Geolocation API, navigator.language , navigator.languages , Date , Intl , and Accept-Language . A site does not have to see a random mixture of a location from one country, a language from another, and a time zone from somewhere else.
 Use realistic data without unnecessary network requests — every Privacy Thing release includes compact local data catalogs built from processed public datasets. Using these catalogs, the extension can independently choose statistically plausible hardware profiles with suitable screen resolutions, CPU-core counts, and available-memory values without making additional requests. Privacy Thing can also rotate the browser version visible to a website. The extension additionally includes catalogs of browser-supported language codes and official languages. These datasets ship with the extension and are refreshed periodically through updates. Privacy Thing does not need to query their sources during normal profile use. A time zone can also be determined locally from coordinates.
 Clear data for a selected website — Privacy Thing can clear data for the current domain, including cookies, localStorage , sessionStorage , IndexedDB , Cache Storage , and service workers. This is useful both for privacy and for testing a website from a clean state. Once the operation finishes, the profile receives an entirely different set of parameters, which should make it significantly harder for the site to track activity.
 Your data. Your call. 
Profiles, rules, and settings stay locally in your browser. Core features require no Privacy Thing account or backend. The extension does not collect its own telemetry and does not sell data.
Ready-made presets, bundled catalogs, and manually entered coordinates work without map-service requests. Place search and map previews use OpenStreetMap Nominatim and OpenFreeMap only after you choose to enable them.
 Privacy works in layers 
Privacy Thing works at the browser layer. It does not change your public IP address, route or encrypt traffic, or replace a VPN, proxy, or Smart DNS service.
Those tools can complement one another: network tools affect the connection or name-resolution layer, while Privacy Thing controls selected information exposed through browser APIs.
Privacy Thing does not guarantee anonymity or undetectability. Websites may also use IP addresses, account data, sessions, and other information beyond the extension’s control. X-Ray reports activity only in supported areas — it is not a complete audit of everything a website does.

firefox-addons:2835988.name: Secure access to Discord with privacy
firefox-addons:2835988.summary: Secure anonymous access for Discord free communications app that lets you chat with friends and game communities.
firefox-addons:2835988.description:
Cordfy is an extension that provides a secure and anonymous access to Discord. Our application aims to offer users a safe and private way to connect with others on the popular communication platform. Below, you will find a comprehensive overview of our features and the benefits they bring to our users. Users can connect to the platform without revealing any personal information from their PC, ensuring their privacy and security online. Cordfy offers a seamless user experience while protecting their data and identity.
Key Features:
1. Secure and Anonymous Access: Cordfy allows users to create an account without providing any personal information. Their identity remains protected while using the application.
2. End-to-End Encryption: All messages and calls on Cordfy are encrypted to prevent unauthorized access to user conversations.
3. Anti-Tracking: Cordfy blocks tracking technologies to maintain user privacy and prevent third-party data collection.
4. IP Masking: Users’ IP addresses are masked to ensure anonymity while using the application.
5. Access to Discord Features: Users can enjoy all the features that Discord provides, including voice and video calls, text messaging, and community forums.
Overall, our application aims to provide users with a secure and anonymous way to access Discord, enabling them to connect with others without compromising their privacy. We are committed to delivering a safe and reliable platform for communication and community building.
Remember that Discord is a free communications app that lets you share voice, video, and text chat with friends, game communities, and developers. It has hundreds of millions of users, making it one of the most popular ways to connect with people online. Anyone can create a Discord server for free for any number of reasons. You can use it to gather friends together in a group text just generally. Use it to post gifs, share memes and screenshots, or talk about your day. You can stream your game to your friends and publishers often use Discord as a place to share gaming goodies with their communities. You can see concept art, new screenshots, and even be given access to a game on Discord.
A new Discord server will start with a General channel, but admins can create multiple channels for specific reasons. These could include server Announcements and Rules, or specific game-related chats, such as a Fortnite channel. It’s up to the admin and the server users to define. Game Streaming in Discord
You can stream your screen to your Discord pals and community. This isn’t like Twitch, YouTube, or Facebook, where it’s meant to be a public show. It’s more of an advanced version of video chat. You can do it in direct message via the home screen or within a public voice chat on the server. It’s entirely confined to the server and to the channel to which you started to stream. You can use it to share your progress in a game with friends, or to show off some loot, or to ask for assistance. You’re even capable of streaming other screens, such as a paint program. Though you can stream a screen alongside your video stream, you can’t combine the screens to overlay you playing picture-in-picture. Unless you buy Nitro, streaming is limited to 720p and up to 30fps. Nitro users can stream up to their source resolution at up to 60fps.
This extension is like a VPN access but providing workstations at the same time so no change to Discord is performed.

firefox-addons:3011420.name: InfraLens - Security & Inspector
firefox-addons:3011420.summary: InfraLens is a lightweight Firefox security and infrastructure analysis extension that helps inspect HTTP headers, HTTPS security, CSP weaknesses, cookies, redirects, CDN, CMS, TLS, mixed content, and website security posture in real time.
firefox-addons:3011420.description:
InfraLens is a powerful read-only Firefox extension designed for cybersecurity professionals, infrastructure engineers, system administrators, developers, SOC analysts, bug bounty hunters, and privacy-focused users who want to inspect the security posture and infrastructure details of websites directly from the browser.
The extension performs fast real-time analysis of the current webpage without modifying page content, injecting ads, or tracking users.
Key Features:
✔ HTTPS and HTTP Security Status
Instantly identify whether a website uses secure HTTPS connections and review protocol security posture.
✔ Security Header Analysis
Inspect important HTTP security headers including:
• Strict-Transport-Security (HSTS)
• Content-Security-Policy (CSP)
• X-Frame-Options
• X-Content-Type-Options
• Referrer-Policy
• Permissions-Policy
• COOP / COEP / CORP
✔ CSP Weakness Detection
Detect common Content Security Policy weaknesses such as:
• unsafe-inline
• unsafe-eval
• wildcard sources
• missing default-src directives
✔ Mixed Content Detection
Identify both active and passive mixed content issues that can weaken browser security.
✔ Redirect Chain Analysis
View main-frame redirect chains to analyze request flows and security behavior.
✔ Cookie Security Inspection
Review cookie security attributes when exposed by the browser:
• Secure
• HttpOnly
• SameSite
✔ DNS and Infrastructure Insights
Retrieve DNS-based IP information using Firefox DNS APIs and identify:
• CDN providers
• CMS technologies
• Runtime/language indicators
• TLS certificate issuer
• Application version hints
• Themes
• Analytics and tracking platforms
✔ Performance and Response Metrics
Measure page response timing using browser request timestamps.
✔ Security Scoring System
Generate an overall security score and grade for the current webpage.
✔ Export and Reporting
Export analysis results as:
• TXT reports
• JSON reports
✔ Quick Security Tools
Open the current website directly in:
• SecurityHeaders
• SSL Labs
• VirusTotal
• Sucuri SiteCheck
✔ Quick Browser Actions
• Copy cURL command
• Reload current tab
• Hard reload with cache bypass
✔ Privacy Focused Design
InfraLens is designed with a security-first and privacy-focused approach:
• Read-only extension
• No telemetry
• No ads
• No tracking
• No backend server dependency
• No page modification
✔ Lightweight and Fast
Designed for minimal overhead while providing valuable infrastructure and security insights directly inside Firefox.
Ideal For:
• Cybersecurity Researchers
• SOC Analysts
• Penetration Testers
• Infrastructure Administrators
• DevOps Engineers
• Web Developers
• Privacy Enthusiasts
• Security Auditors
• Bug Bounty Hunters
Permissions Usage:
InfraLens uses browser webRequest and related permissions only to inspect response headers and request metadata of the currently visited page for security analysis purposes.
No user browsing data is sold, tracked, or transmitted externally.
Developed by NB InfoTech.

firefox-addons:2972834.name: LockMyTab – Secure PIN Lock for Tabs
firefox-addons:2972834.summary: Protect your privacy by locking individual browser tabs with a secure 4-digit PIN. Secure, fast, and easy to use.
firefox-addons:2972834.description:
Protect your privacy and secure sensitive information with LockMyTab, the ultimate PIN-protected browser extension for Chrome, Edge, and Firefox. 
Designed for professionals, students, and privacy-conscious users, LockMyTab allows you to lock individual browser tabs behind a secure 4-digit PIN, ensuring your data remains hidden from prying eyes, even when you share your device.
Key Features:
- Secure 4-Digit PIN: Instantly lock any tab with a simple numeric code.
- Automatic Auto-Lock: Set an idle timer to automatically re-lock protected tabs when you step away.
- Full Content Masking: Prevents viewing, copying, or interacting with tab content using a high-fidelity blur screen.
- Selective Security: Lock only the tabs you need. Protect specific websites without affecting the rest of your browsing speed.
- Quick Shortcut: Use Alt+L to lock your current tab in an instant.
- Recovery Keys: Never get locked out! We provide 3 secure recovery pins during setup.
- Minimalist & High-End Interface: A distraction-free, glassmorphism-inspired lock screen that integrates seamlessly with your workflow.
Why Choose LockMyTab?
Whether you are handling confidential client data, managing personal bank accounts, or simply want to keep your social media private, LockMyTab provides that essential extra layer of security. It’s perfect for open-plan offices, shared home computers, or anyone who values digital privacy.
How to use:
1. Click the LockMyTab icon or press Alt+L on any tab you want to secure.
2. Enter your custom PIN to unlock and access the content.
3. Manage your PIN and Auto-Lock settings easily from the Options page.

firefox-addons:3106853.name: WebTool Inspector
firefox-addons:3106853.summary: Inspect any site: detected technologies & versions, IP/ASN/geo, WHOIS/RDAP, DNS, TLS certificate and HTTP security headers — in one Firefox popup.
firefox-addons:3106853.description:
WebTool Inspector is a Firefox toolkit for everyday web investigation and development.
Open the toolbar button on any http(s) page to get:
• Overview — hosting, technologies, certificate and security headers at a glance
• Tech — 500+ signatures (CMS, frameworks, CDNs, analytics…) with versions when available
• IP / ASN — contacted IP, geolocation, ASN/ISP, reverse DNS, IP RDAP
• Domain — registrar, dates, DNSSEC, nameservers + A/AAAA/NS/MX/SPF/DMARC/CAA/SOA
• Certificate — TLS version, cipher, SAN, key, fingerprints, chain, PEM export
• Headers — redirect chain, security-header checklist, info-leak headers, raw response
Also includes quick links to OSINT tools (Shodan, Censys, VirusTotal, crt.sh , SSL Labs, and more), prefilled with the current host / IP / ASN.
Privacy: lookups for DNS (Cloudflare DoH), RDAP and IP geo contact third-party services. See the privacy policy. No accounts, no ads, no telemetry SDK.

apple-macos:6794546268.name: Frelio
apple-macos:6794546268.description:
Field notes for your friendships.
Some people are worth remembering, and we forget them anyway. The church planter with three kids and a fishing habit. The barista who knows your order before you say it. Frelio is a pocket notebook for the people in your life. Part field notes on the ones you're just getting to know, part gentle nudge to keep showing up for the ones you already love.
It's not a social network. There's no feed, and nobody to perform for. The phone comes out for five seconds so the next conversation can go deeper.
JUST MET SOMEONE?
Jot their name and one detail. That's it. Dictate it in the parking lot if your hands are full. Next time you see them, you'll remember the thing that mattered, and they'll notice that you did.
AT A CONFERENCE OR A WEDDING?
Start an event and everyone you meet files under it automatically. Afterwards, Frelio runs a quick memory game on who you met, because saying a name out loud is how it sticks. Open that event a year later and everyone's still there.
YOUR CIRCLE
The handful of people you're really investing in get more. Birthdays. A check-in rhythm that fits each person, weekly for your closest, quarterly for the old roommate across the country. A quiet nudge when life has crowded somebody out. No streaks and no guilt.
PLACES
Friendship has a geography. Your city, your church, the gym, the coffee shop. Add your spots and Frelio keeps track of who you meet there. Your regulars become your people.
ON EVERY DEVICE
Keep your notebook on every device, and get new features first. Create a Frelio account and your iPhone, iPad and Mac stay in step. Sign in with Apple or Google. An account is optional. Without one, Frelio works the way it always has.
ALSO IN THE BOX
One-tap capture from your lock screen. Siri can add someone for you, and so can your Apple Watch. Save people to your iPhone Contacts without creating duplicates. Photos, common ground, search across everything you've written, and a full export of your notebook anytime.
PRIVATE, ACTUALLY
Your notebook lives on your device. Frelio has no ads, and nothing in it tracks you across other apps or websites.
Create a Frelio account and your notebook is encrypted on your device before it leaves, so nobody else can read it, us included. Your Apple account keeps the key safe, and you get a recovery key for the rare day you need it. What Frelio can see is short: your email, your first name if you give it, the devices you use, and a few counts and dates.
One more thing Frelio won't do: become your brain. Writing a detail down is an act of paying attention. The goal is that you remember the name next time, not that an app remembers it for you.
